subject: Sustained deferment & error spike — CloudPoint production impact
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@cloudpoint.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in tail latency and 5xxs — urgent

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing sustained failures yesterday evening (Nov 21) and the issue has persisted this morning. Our monitoring shows p99 climb from ~1.1s to ~12s on our production route, and a 5xx/error rate of roughly 7–9% across requests to the /generate endpoint. Throughput is nominal, but a large fraction of requests is timing out on completion. This is causing transactions to fail in our checkout flow (we're seeing abandoned carts).

We've attached a small set of request samples and a short set of debug logs for the last 2 hours (request_samples.json / debug_log_20261122.txt). We did not change our traffic profile — this looks like something on the inference side. Can Redwood confirm root cause and an ETA for mitigation? We are within an active quarter and this is causing significant revenue impact.

Elena
Customer Ops | CloudPoint

Attachments:
- request_samples.json (json)
- debug_log_20261122.txt (text)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:26:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in tail latency and 5xxs — urgent

Team — escalating: CloudPoint (CP-9347) reporting sustained p99 ~12s and ~8% error rate on /generate. They report no traffic changes. Files attached in original.

Immediate asks:
- Dev: can you triage pool-level queueing and concurrency limits (check autoscaler thresholds + OOMs) and validate whether prefix/KV cache regressions are present. Prioritize logs for the time window in Elena's samples.
- Hannah: CS please prep a brief customer note with expected next steps & temporary mitigations. Keep Elena in the loop; she flagged business impact.
- Marissa: FYI — may need exec attention if mitigation isn't quick.

I'll coordinate comms with the customer. Please reply with ETA and any quick mitigations you can apply without rolling models.

-Jordan
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in tail latency and 5xxs — urgent

Quick triage update (first 35m):
- Reproduced spike in request samples — significant queueing observed on the customers' serving shard set around 2026-11-21T22:40Z.
- Observed worker concurrency cap hitting soft limit (configured cap=16) and autoscaler lag in adding GPUs; backlog grew and KV cache churned (miss ratio up ~2.6x).
- No OOMs or model crashes recorded; workers remained healthy but saturated (long queue residence times).

Immediate mitigations I can do without a model rollout (ETA ~30–45m):
1) Open a temporary dedicated worker pool for CP traffic and route their prefix to it (will isolate and remove cross-tenant noisy neighbors).
2) Raise concurrency cap for CP's pool from 16 -> 48 (short window, monitored).
3) Enable aggressive prefix-level KV cache retention for their model to reduce cold cache misses.
4) Apply a short per-token rate soft-limit to smooth bursts (sliding window) — avoids head-of-line blocking while maintaining throughput.

I'll attach first-pass logs (debug_log_20261122.txt) and a short mitigation_runbook.pdf. If the dedicated pool is approved, provisioning + warmup should finish in ~20–30m.

- Dev (Infra / Serving Runtime)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Exec readout request — CloudPoint production impact (p99 12s, 8% 5xx)

Marissa — short readout and asks so you can decide whether to loop in Ops/Rev: 

Impact summary:
- Customer: CloudPoint (CP-9347) — production p99 up to ~12s, 5xxs ~7–9% over the last 12h; checkout failures reported.
- Scope: affects a single high-traffic model route; requests are queuing on the shared serving pool.
- No model regressions detected yet; root cause appears operational (queueing / concurrency caps + cache churn).

Requested actions:
1) Approve immediate creation of a temporary dedicated pool for CloudPoint traffic (cost ~short-term GPU-hours). Dev indicates warmup ~20–30m.
2) Approve an emergency credit of up to $10k (one-time) to offset customer losses & goodwill if we need to expedite capacity or offer billing relief.

If you approve both, we will: provision the pool, apply concurrency cap increase, enable KV cache retention, and send a customer-facing mitigation note with monitoring thresholds. Dev will provide a post-mortem and proposed long-term fixes (dedicated commit, model quantization, tighter autoscaler heuristics).

I recommend we authorize the above now; without the dedicated pool risk of repeat spikes exists. Hannah will lead the customer communication.

-Jordan
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@cloudpoint.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in tail latency and 5xxs — mitigation update

Elena — quick update and next steps: 

What we did (completed):
- Provisioned a temporary dedicated serving pool for CloudPoint and routed your production prefix to it.
- Increased concurrency cap for the pool from 16 -> 48 and enabled stronger KV cache retention for the model.
- Applied a short sliding-window per-token smoothing rule to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Early results (30–60m post-mitigation):
- p99 has dropped from ~12s -> ~1.9s on the routed pool.
- 5xx rate down from ~8% -> ~0.5%.
- No increased error surface observed from the mitigations; throughput stable.

Next steps (48h plan):
- Monitor closely for 48h; we'll keep the dedicated pool live while we assess long-term options.
- Engineering (Dev) will deliver a short post-mortem with root cause timeline and recommended durable fixes: either a Dedicated commit for CloudPoint, model quantization guidance, or autoscaler tuning to prevent future lag.
- CS (Hannah) will coordinate a short executive call to discuss credits and SLA impacts.

We appreciate the heads-up and are treating this as high priority. I'll share the runbook and final post-mortem when ready.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
